strengths: The problem has an identifiable audience in contextual bandits and Bayesian optimization. Combining changing arm availability, combinatorial constraints, and correlated mean outcomes addresses a useful learning setting.

The algorithm cleanly separates learning from combinatorial optimization through an approximation oracle. Lemma 2 convincingly connects approximation regret to selected-arm confidence widths under the stated monotonicity and Lipschitz assumptions.

The experiments examine coverage, crowdsourcing, and varying outcome correlation. Inducing-point sweeps, runtime measurements, and repeated runs provide useful evidence about the empirical tradeoff between approximation quality and computation.
weaknesses: Necessary theoretical correction: The information-gain lower bound in Theorem 3/Theorem 6 needs additional feasibility assumptions. Equation (A33) replaces optimization over feasible super-arm sequences with unrestricted context sequences; constant availability does not justify this. For example, take K=T=1, X={a,b}, only {a} feasible, independent GP values with variances 0.1 and 1, and noise variance 1. Then gamma_bar_1=0.5 log(1.1), whereas gamma_1=0.5 log(2), contradicting the stated lower bound. Restrict the theorem and provide a valid proof, or remove this claim. Equation (A34) also uses posterior variance after the current observation, whereas the information-gain identity requires variance before it.

Necessary proof clarification: Lemma 3 treats the absence of internal algorithmic randomization as making selected contexts deterministic (pp. 24–25). Selections still depend on noisy observations. Consequently, the Gaussian entropy calculation in (A11)–(A12) requires more careful treatment of conditioning and expectations. The main upper-bound argument appears repairable using a pathwise log-determinant identity for each realized design, but the supplied proof must establish that argument explicitly.

Necessary modeling clarification: The application examples do not consistently satisfy the formal model. Coverage uses Bernoulli observations and probabilities in [0,1], while the theory assumes Gaussian observations and GP-distributed means. Explain how valid probabilities are supplied to TIM+ and clearly identify the sparse, randomized-oracle experiment as outside the proved guarantee. Also, K=3 counts movies in this experiment, whereas the theoretical K bounds selected base arms, which are edges here. The crowdsourcing log reward can be undefined under Gaussian noise; specify the actual noise support or reward transformation and how expected regret is computed. A new theorem for every practical variant is unnecessary if these distinctions are explicit.

Necessary claim qualification: Agreement with an approximate TIM+ benchmark does not establish the 'optimal performance' claimed in Section 5.1.3. The results support improvements on the specified semi-synthetic benchmarks. Likewise, the runtime comparison supports acceleration of the reported implementation, but the O(K^3 T^4) exact-GP cost assumes repeated reconstruction; incremental updates are available. Figure 5 still shows several minutes per sparse-GP round at T=250, so suitability for large simulations or online use needs qualification. Comparisons of theoretical rates should also acknowledge the different assumptions imposed on the unknown function.

Necessary reporting corrections: Section 5.4.1 prints an exponential of an unsquared distance, which is not the claimed squared-exponential kernel; clarify which kernel generated the results. Specify the sparse posterior implementation and likelihood sufficiently to distinguish inducing-variable inference using all observations from fitting only a subsample. Resolve the 250-versus-300-round descriptions. Equation (1) also needs the prior-mean terms or an explicit zero-mean assumption. These issues affect interpretation and reproducibility beyond ordinary proofreading.

Optional improvements: Kernel-sensitivity experiments, longer-horizon runtime measurements, and comparison with an incrementally updated exact GP would improve practical guidance. These are not prerequisites if the empirical and scalability claims are appropriately narrowed.
